# Mwila Hilton Mwaba

<p class="tagline">Biopharmaceutical scientist and lecturer working on pharmacogenomics, structural biology and implementation science for non-communicable diseases, and writing about how health research is produced, governed and taught in Zambia.</p>

::: {.home-body}

<p class="intro">I am a Lecturer in the Basic Sciences Department at the Michael Chilufya Sata School of Medicine, Copperbelt University, where I have taught since 2019 and coordinate undergraduate research. My doctorate in Pharmaceutical Sciences is from Hokkaido University, Japan. This site collects my essays, the projects I am currently leading, and my publications.</p>

## What I do

:::: {.card-grid}

::: {.card}
<span class="tag">Research</span>

### Evidence and where it comes from

Computational and structural approaches to drug targets, with a continuing interest in who produces health evidence in Zambia, and where.
:::

::: {.card}
<span class="tag">Teaching</span>

### Biomedical sciences

Immunology and related assessments for BSc Biomedical Sciences students, including the fourth-year MBM 425 examination.
:::

::: {.card}
<span class="tag">Leadership</span>

### Programmes and networks

Programme development for pharmacogenomics, Work Package 5 of IS4NCDs, and the African Bioethics Network in Zambia.
:::

::::
